result.topic_en: Euler states Theorem IX, which turns a general alternating series into a continued fraction, and begins an example: he expands the integral Z = ∫ z^{m-1} dz (1+z^n)^{k/n-1} as v(1+z^n)^{k/n} and finds the power-series coefficients of v.
result.transcription:
170
Theorema IX.
§. 51. Si proposita fuerit ista series generalis:
$s = \frac{ax}{\alpha y} - \frac{abxx}{\alpha\beta yy} + \frac{abcx^3}{\alpha\beta\gamma y^3} - \frac{abcdx^4}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta y^4} + \text{etc.}$
inde formabitur fractio continua
$\frac{ax}{s} = \alpha y + \cfrac{\alpha bxy}{\beta y - bx + \cfrac{\beta cxy}{\gamma y - cx + \cfrac{\gamma dxy}{\delta y - dx + \text{etc.}}}}$
§. 52. Vt hoc Theorema per exemplum notatu dignum illustremus, consideremus hanc formulam integralem:
$Z = \int z^{m-1} dz (1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}-1}$
quod integrale ita sumatur vt euanescat posito $z = 0$, ac statuamus $Z = v(1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}}$, eritque differentiando
$dZ = z^{m-1}dz(1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}-1} = dv(1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}}$
$+ kvz^{n-1}dz(1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}-1}$,
quae aequatio per $(1+z^n)^{\frac{k}{n}-1}$ diuisa praebet
$z^{m-1}dz = dv(1+z^n) + kvz^{n-1}dz$, ideoque
$\frac{dv}{dz}(1+z^n) + kvz^{n-1} - z^{m-1} = 0$.
§. 53. Quoniam sumto $z$ infinite paruo fit
$Z = \frac{z^m}{m} = v$,
inde discimus, quantitatem $v$ per eiusmodi seriem infinitam exprimi, cuius primus terminus sit potestas $z^m$; in sequen-

171
tibus autem terminis exponentes ipsius $z$ continuo numero $n$ augeri, quamobrem pro $v$ fingamus sequentem seriem infinitam:
$v = Az^m - Bz^{m+n} + Cz^{m+2n} - Dz^{m+3n} + \text{etc.}$
quem valorem in aequatione differentiali substituamus, similesque potestates ipsius $z$ sibi subscribamus sequenti modo:
$\frac{dv}{dz} = mAz^{m-1} - (m+n)Bz^{m+n-1} + (m+2n)Cz^{m+2n-1} - (m+3n)Dz^{m+3n-1} + \text{etc.}$
$\frac{z^n dv}{dz} = \quad + mA \quad - (m+n)B \quad + (m+2n)C - \text{etc.}$
$+ kvz^{n-1} = + kA \quad - kB \quad + kC$
$- z^{m-1} = - 1.$
§. 54. Quod si nunc singulae ipsius $z$ potestates seorsim ad nihilum redigantur, obtinebuntur sequentes valores:
$mA - 1 = 0$ ergo $A = \frac{1}{m}$
$-(m+n)B + (m+k)A = 0$ ergo $B = \frac{(m+k)A}{m+n}$
$(m+2n)C - (m+n+k)B = 0$ ergo $C = \frac{(m+n+k)B}{m+2n}$
$-(m+3n)D + (m+2n+k)C = 0$ ergo $D = \frac{(m+2n+k)C}{m+3n}$
etc. etc.
§. 55. Substituamus igitur hos valores inuentos ac pro $v$ reperiemus sequentem seriem infinitam:
$v = \frac{z^m}{m} - \frac{m+k}{m(m+n)}z^{m+n} + \frac{(m+k)(m+n+k)}{m(m+n)(m+2n)}z^{m+2n}$
$- \frac{(m+k)(m+n+k)(m+2n+k)}{m(m+n)(m+2n)(m+3n)}z^{m+3n}$ etc.

items.quote: Si proposita fuerit ista series generalis: $s = \frac{ax}{\alpha y} - \frac{abxx}{\alpha\beta yy} + \frac{abcx^3}{\alpha\beta\gamma y^3} - \frac{abcdx^4}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta y^4} + \text{etc.}$ inde formabitur fractio continua
items.english: If this general series is proposed, s = ax/(αy) − abx²/(αβy²) + abcx³/(αβγy³) − ..., then the continued fraction ax/s = αy + αbxy/(βy − bx + βcxy/(γy − cx + ...)) is formed from it.

items.quote: Vt hoc Theorema per exemplum notatu dignum illustremus, consideremus hanc formulam integralem
items.english: To illustrate this theorem with a noteworthy example, let us consider this integral formula.
